messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 12:03 UTC - Elevated 429/500 errors from ratelimit-worker (prod). Suspected upstream provider: upstash (EU region). Paging oncall.
ashley: taking pager — seeing a big spike in 429s from calls to upstash REST endpoint (eu). Clients hitting token-bucket checks get 429s, auth cache misses up too.
ashley: sample backend trace: `redis-client -> POST https://eu.upstash.io/v1/command/incr -> 429 Retry-After: 30`
linda: logs show `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` from upstash and a burst of `ERR ServiceUnavailable` in the ratelimit worker. Rate limiter failing open would be bad.
raj: oncall here, taking lead. rough customer impact?
ashley: initial graphs: ~12% of user-facing requests in eu-1 hitting 429s for ~8 mins. Affected flows: login token validation and rate-limited API endpoints. Some webhook retries piling up.
ops: upstash-status posted: "We are investigating increased latency and rate limiting affecting REST API in eu-central-1" (12:04 UTC).
ashley: mitigation plan: 1) enable local in-process rate-limit fallback, 2) pause noncritical writes to upstash (metrics/telemetry), 3) increase token-cache TTL to reduce reads. Rolling canary now (10% of traffic).
ashley: command run: `rbctl feature-toggle set ratelimit.local_fallback=true --env prod --canary 10`
ashley: also paused `metrics-flusher` jobs to stop background write pressure: `systemctl stop metrics-flusher.service`
raj: canary results: errors on canary hosts dropped from 18% -> 1.5% within 90s. Good signal.
linda: after fallback enabled globally, we see most 429s disappear. Still see occasional 500s from the provider for heavy multi-key ops.
ashley: temporary config change: token cache TTL from 60s -> 300s to reduce auth reads to upstash. `config set auth.token_ttl 300` (rolling restart of auth-cache instances).
ashley: note: fallback mode uses approx +10% CPU on ratelimit workers, but latency stays within SLO.
ops: preparing customer comms. Draft: "We detected transient rate-limit errors due to an upstream provider incident in EU, mitigation applied, services returning to normal. Working on root cause and follow-ups."
raj: handing off monitoring to me for the next 30m. I'll create the incident ticket and assign postmortem owners.
raj: creating PROD-3241 with summary, timeline, and action items (local fallback runbook, circuit breaker improvements, synthetic monitors).
upstash-status: We've identified a misapplied global rate-limit on some REST API keys in eu-central-1; mitigation in progress. We will post updates.
linda: postmortem action items (quick list): 1) Add automated circuit-breaker on upstream 429s -> trigger local fallback, 2) Add per-region synthetic writes to detect provider throttling, 3) Reduce reliance on single-region managed cache for critical auth path, 4) Add account-level impact report for top 20 customers.
ashley: agree. Also: add metric to track how often fallback is hit (counter + alert).
ops: severity set to Sev2 and support notified. Support to draft targeted customer emails for any customers who reported errors.
raj: update 12:18 UTC - error rates back to baseline after global rollout of fallback and pausing metrics. Monitoring for 30m.
ashley: handing off to raj at 12:11 UTC for monitoring and follow-ups — I'll join postmortem.
raj: will keep watch, will escalate if external provider posts major update. Adding timeline notes to PROD-3241.
incident-bot: Incident PROD-3241 updated: status -> monitoring.
upstash-status: 12:25 UTC - Partial mitigation applied. Some API keys still subject to throttling; we recommend retry/backoff.
linda: 12:30 UTC - metrics show stable, 429s at baseline. Preparing actions for postmortem.
raj: closing pager if no regressions in next 30m; postmortem to include exact affected customer list and estimated error counts.
nashley: thanks everyone for quick coordination — follow-ups in PROD-3241. :thumbsup:
